newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- PRICES END EVEN TO UP SLIGHTLY.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- PRICES END EVEN TO UP SLIGHTLY.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended unchanged to 1/8 point higher Wednesday as the gloom cast by Friday's sell off began to lift, and players mulled the fate of new municipal and government market supply.

"We had a whole preponderance of new issues this week. I don't think they were all that robustly received," a municipal trader said. "You've got the Treasury auction which is two-thirds of the way done, and I'm not sure anybody really knows what the story is there yet."

The U.S. Treasury sold $12 billion in 10-year notes, Wednesday afternoon, completing the second leg of its quarterly refunding. The notes were sold at an average yield of 6.205 percent. The government is scheduled to sell $10 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
"We're still waiting for something," a trader said. "The market seemed to lose a lot of its sponsorship over the last week after Friday."

The bond market sold off Friday after strong news on employment and manufacturing. On Wednesday, the benchmark 30-year bond was trading up 5/32 at 101-29/32 to yield 6.48 percent in late New York trade.
In debt futures, the September municipal contact closed up 4/32 at 120-17/32. The September T-bond contract closed up 5/32 at 114-24/32. The MOB spread was 185 ticks.

Turning to new issues, EVEREN Securities repriced Rochester Community School District, Mich.'s $101 million bond offering, lowering yields in several maturities. The offering's top yield of 5.375 percent in 2017 remained unchanged.

Also Wednesday, Morgan Stanley Dean Witter released the retail scale for a $464 million Allegheny County, Pa., airport revenue refunding bond deal. The top yield was set at 5.53 percent in 2016. When the retail order period ended 1500 EDT Wednesday, about $14 million of orders had been received, an underwriting source said.
